title: Anti-CD20 Therapy Within the Early High-Efficacy Treatment Paradigm in GCC Multiple Sclerosis: Evidence, Clinical Positioning, and a Regional Treatment-Sequencing Framework
content: Background: Anti-CD20 monoclonal antibodies are central to high-efficacy multiple sclerosis (MS) care. Across the six Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) states, clinical value also depends on infection prevention, reproductive planning, delivery capacity, mixed public-private coverage, tender continuity, biosimilar governance, and registry maturity. Objectives: To map anti-CD20 efficacy, safety, real-world, reproductive, pharmacoeconomic, access, biosimilar, and implementation evidence, and translate it into a GCC treatment-sequencing and monitoring framework. Methods: PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, the Cochrane Library, Google Scholar, registries, regulatory sources, conference materials and relevant grey literature were searched through 8 July 2026. Two reviewers screened titles/abstracts and full-text reports independently and resolved disagreements by consensus, as described in the original review methods. A targeted evidence update through 13 October 2026 informed clinical interpretation without changing the original review counts. Results: Searches identified 1,870 records; 550 duplicates were removed, 1,320 records screened, 270 full-text reports assessed and 95 sources included. Pivotal and extension studies support the anti-inflammatory efficacy of ocrelizumab, ofatumumab and ublituximab. OVERLORD-MS adds randomized head-to-head MRI non-inferiority evidence for rituximab versus ocrelizumab. The October evidence update includes a seven-country MENACTRIMS rituximab cohort (n = 774), a Kuwaiti high-efficacy treatment cohort (n = 1,408), additional immunoglobulin and safety data, and emerging Saudi and UAE clinical reports. GCC implementation priorities include treatment continuity, affordability, reproductive care, biosimilar governance and registry development [80–88]. Conclusions: The proposed framework positions anti-CD20 therapy selectively within early high-efficacy care, integrating inflammatory risk, agent-specific evidence and safety, reproductive planning, route preference, access continuity, biosimilar traceability, and registry capture. OVERLORD-MS strengthens rituximab’s comparative evidence but does not establish class-wide interchangeability. Prospective multicountry GCC validation remains necessary.
